nodes.detailed_figure_description: Hand-drawn voltage-versus-time graph. The vertical axis is labeled V and the horizontal axis t(s). A periodic sinusoidal-like waveform oscillates about the horizontal axis between dashed levels labeled V₀ and −V₀. An orange bracket beneath the graph marks the horizontal extent of “1 cycle.”
nodes.figure_alternative: AC voltage waveform ranging from −V₀ to V₀, with one cycle marked.

nodes.spoken_math_alternative: V equals V naught times sine of omega t.

nodes.figure_alternative: Hand-drawn loop containing a resistor, capacitor, and circular sine-wave source symbol. An arrow identifies the circle as the “circuit symbol for AC voltage source.”

nodes.spoken_math_alternative: Sixty cycles per second times two pi radians per cycle equals three hundred seventy-seven radians per second.
V R M S equals the square root of the average of V squared.

nodes.text: FACT: the average value of sin² θ (or cos² θ) over a cycle is 1/2.

nodes.detailed_figure_description: Hand-drawn graph with vertical axis y, horizontal axis t, and a vertical-axis mark at 1. A sequence of rounded, predominantly nonnegative lobes begins at zero and returns to the time axis between lobes. The curve is labeled “Sin(ωt).”
nodes.figure_alternative: Time graph labeled Sin(ωt), drawn as repeated positive lobes between zero and one.

nodes.spoken_math_alternative: The average of sine squared of omega t equals one half.

V R M S equals the square root of the average of V naught squared times sine squared of omega t, which equals the square root of V naught squared times one half, which equals V naught divided by the square root of two.
V R M S equals V naught divided by the square root of two.

warnings.message: The lower graph is labeled “Sin(ωt),” but its repeated nonnegative lobes and the surrounding discussion of the average of sin²(ωt) suggest that the intended label may be sin²(ωt).
